items.title: AI safety fears put OpenAI and Anthropic in the FTC's crosshairs
items.excerpt: An FTC spokesperson confirmed to Axios the agency is investigating OpenAI, Anthropic and other AI companies over potential safety risks of their products; per the New York Post, Chair Andrew Ferguson is preparing civil investigative demands compelling documents and testimony. Probe predates the Hugging Face incident disclosure.

items.title: Federal appeals court upholds Thomson Reuters' landmark AI copyright win
items.excerpt: The 3rd U.S. Circuit affirmed Thomson Reuters' win over Ross Intelligence — the first federal appeals ruling to reject fair use for training a commercial AI product on publisher content without permission; Judge Montgomery-Reeves noted the case did not involve an LLM or generative AI, possibly limiting its reach.

items.title: "An AI did it" is no defense, says nonprofit suing OpenAI over Hugging Face hack
items.excerpt: Nonprofit LASST sued OpenAI in San Francisco County Superior Court under California's CDAFA and Unfair Competition Law over the July Hugging Face hack, seeking an injunction barring its AI agents from unauthorized access; OpenAI calls the suit 'completely without merit'.

items.title: Streamlining Access to Government Services Through America.gov
items.excerpt: Executive order establishes America.gov as a conversational 'digital front door' to federal services and requires that super intelligence used with it be accurate, reliable and transparent; OMB has 90 days to issue implementation guidance. Primary document.

items.title: Trump launches America.gov with AI chatbots at its core
items.excerpt: America.gov launches with Google Gemini and xAI Grok chatbots trained on 29,000 government websites; most transactional features slated for 2027. Same event as the EO.

items.title: Ask Trump's AI chatbot who won in 2020. You might not get an answer.
items.excerpt: America.gov's chatbot gave inconsistent answers to politically sensitive questions; same America.gov thread.

items.title: EU to Trump: We will keep pushing for global AI safety rules
items.excerpt: EU tech chief Henna Virkkunen said the Commission will keep seeking an international AI safety and security agreement despite U.S. opposition, backing the Finland/Norway-led international safety body initiative signed by 20 other countries.

items.title: Huawei boss claims homegrown AI chip sales top Nvidia in China
items.excerpt: Huawei rotating chairman Eric Xu claimed Ascend NPUs have surpassed Nvidia's share in China, framing chip self-sufficiency as the path forward amid shifting U.S. export controls.

items.title: Will Chinese AI companies slow down? A top House Democrat wants answers
items.excerpt: Rep. Ro Khanna sent letters to ODNI and to DeepSeek, Alibaba and Moonshot AI asking about incident preparedness, superintelligence/RSI efforts, kill switches and openness to inspections under a possible US-China treaty.

items.title: What Counts as Scientific Research? The EU's Digital Omnibus Could Set the Definition
items.excerpt: Parliament amendments to the Digital Omnibus GDPR 'scientific research' definition split between explicitly including and excluding AI development, training and testing.

items.title: AI Transparency Starts With the Audience
items.excerpt: Partnership on AI authors argue AI disclosure rules should be designed around each audience; commentary on PAI's disclosure recommendations.

items.title: AI companies want to embed safety evaluators, but countries need their own
items.excerpt: After OpenAI agent incidents incl. the Australian health database access, experts at a Rest of World event urged countries to run their own AI safety evaluations.

items.title: Who's liable when AI agents go rogue?
items.excerpt: Explainer: state AI transparency laws (SB 53, RAISE Act, Illinois SB 315) define critical incidents narrowly, so OpenAI likely wasn't required to disclose its agents' hacks; liability paths analyzed.
